clue.text: To suppress frauds they'll be needed in court

parts.note: to squash a rebellion is to suppress it
rackets are dishonest schemes or swindles

explanation.surface: Instruments needed by a court to crack down on swindlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is the squash court where the game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Players carry these bats onto a squash court, so they are court equipment in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Five players still not inwardly disheartened

indicators.note: inwardly says the next piece is placed within the word for still

parts.note: still means quiet, silent

indicators.note: disheartened means the word not loses its central letter, its heart

explanation.surface: Five musicians remain cheerful in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle letter from the clue word, and 'inwardly' puts what is left within the word for still; 'still' is an adjective here, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of five musicians performing together is called by this musical term.

clue.text: Performs religious work

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for performing and the short title of a New Testament book.

clue.text: They may rise up in anger

definitions.text: They may rise up in anger

parts.words: They may rise up in anger
parts.note: an angry person's ... are said to rise, like a dog's raised neck hairs

explanation.definitionFit: These are the neck hairs of an animal, raised when it is angry, giving the idiom of hackles rising.

clue.text: Bill, a relation

definitions.meaning: a bill is a statement of charges owed
a relation is a narrative or report of events

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an invoice of money owed and a narrated report of what happened.

clue.text: It may be tied for speed at sea

definitions.text: It may be tied for speed at sea

parts.words: It may be tied for speed at sea
parts.note: the word is both a tied loop of rope and a nautical unit of speed

explanation.definitionFit: A tied loop in rope shares its name with the nautical mile per hour used at sea.

clue.text: It doesn't normally contain mother's ruin

definitions.text: It doesn't normally contain mother's ruin

indicators.note: ruin, read as a verb, tells us to wreck the order of the letters before it

parts.note: taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: A vacuum flask is not usually filled with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother's ruin' is British slang for gin; read cryptically, 'ruin' scrambles MOTHERS, and the whole clue describes the flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask usually holds tea or coffee rather than gin, so the whole sentence describes one.

clue.text: It's used to make pictures or compare a thing differently

indicators.note: differently says the letters are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A film camera, or a matter of weighing one thing against another.
explanation.definitionFit: This early machine both shot and projected moving pictures.

clue.text: Fast-moving drug dealer

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun phrase meaning a fast-moving person

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a merchant is a dealer in goods

explanation.surface: A drug pusher always on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for someone who drives, runs or bowls very fast.

clue.text: Dot three i's in various places, many being silly

indicators.note: in various places tells us to scatter the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: three letters I written together
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Dotting lots of letters i all over the place seems foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in various places' rearranges the dot and the three letters; 'many' is the Roman hundred, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foolish or stupid behaviour is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Photograph way-out couples

indicators.note: way-out means weird or unconventional, so the letters go out of order

explanation.surface: A picture of eccentric pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture taken from very near the subject is called this.

clue.text: Amphibians with feet going in two directions

indicators.note: going in places the abbreviation for feet within the two compass letters

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Creatures whose feet head two ways at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts, especially young ones, are called by this old word.

clue.text: Hit 150 before getting dismissed

indicators.note: before puts the numeral ahead of the next piece

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A batsman hits a big score of 150 before getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is a decoy: 150 is Roman CL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a heavy blow or a smack.

clue.text: Duck! It's Captain Hook's bosun!

definitions.meaning: an old dialect name for a kind of duck such as the wigeon
in Peter Pan, Captain Hook's boatswain is called this

explanation.definitionFit: A dialect duck name that is also the bosun of the pirate ship in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Direction followed by ship's complement that drives it

indicators.note: followed by sets the next piece after the compass letter

parts.note: S is the compass point south
a ship's complement is its crew

explanation.surface: The heading followed by the sailors who run the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is called its screw, the device that pushes it through water.

clue.text: Sharp crooked instruments

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Cunning, dishonest tools.
explanation.definitionFit: These stringed musical instruments are plucked by hand.

clue.text: Criticises VAT in speech?

indicators.note: in speech says the words are judged by how they are said

parts.note: VAT is a tax, so a tax

explanation.surface: Is the sales tax being complained about verbally?
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK value added tax; 'a tax' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to attack an idea is to criticise it strongly.

clue.text: It may appear as smart on the stern of a boat

indicators.note: may appear as says the letters show up in another form

explanation.surface: Something looking smart on the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat transverse board forming the back of a boat is this part.

clue.text: He got on in new form, being energetic

indicators.note: in new form says the letters are recast in another arrangement

explanation.surface: He made progress, looking reinvigorated and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone always busy and active is said to be constantly in motion like this.

clue.text: Advertisement that's attached to back of vehicle

definitions.meaning: a film preview advertising a coming film

definitions.text: that's attached to back of vehicle
definitions.meaning: a wheeled cart towed behind a car or lorry

explanation.definitionFit: Both a preview of a coming film and a towed wheeled cart.

clue.text: One's naughty spirit as an individual

parts.note: taken as written, the S kept
an elf is a small mischievous spirit

explanation.surface: A person's mischievous inner sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun refers to a person on their own, an individual.

clue.text: More changes put around by ruler

indicators.note: put around says the shuffled letters are placed round the next piece
changes says the letters are altered in order

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: More alterations brought in by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the clue's first word into EMOR, and 'put around' wraps those letters about the Latin word for by.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Carries out personal property

definitions.meaning: to effect a plan is to carry it out

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for bringing about and a noun for one's belongings.

clue.text: Become aware of the facts about a tissue of lies

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a tissue is a woven thing, so the letters are woven into new order

explanation.surface: Discover the truth about a web of deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tissue of' weaves the letters into ALISE; a tissue of lies is a web of falsehoods, so the surface reads as idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to come to understand the truth of something.

clue.text: Romany loses my horse

indicators.note: loses says the next letters are taken out of the first word

explanation.surface: A gypsy traveller loses the horse he owns.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs is called this.

clue.text: Muscular like some bully?

definitions.meaning: bully beef is tinned corned beef, so it is beef-like

explanation.definitionFit: Means brawny, and also describes bully beef, which is corned beef.

clue.text: A number remains — so hurry!

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A count of what is left over, so get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rush or go somewhere quickly.

clue.text: Don't answer a question but have exam success

definitions.meaning: on a quiz, saying ... declines to answer
to ... an exam is to succeed in it

explanation.definitionFit: Both declining a turn to answer and succeeding in a test.

clue.text: Working with the Church in former times

parts.note: on means working or operating
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Employed by the church in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: formerly, at one time in the past.

clue.text: Convict dividing hoard and plunder

indicators.note: dividing says the convict splits the hoard into two parts

parts.note: a pile is a heap, a hoard
a lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner shares out the stash and the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plunder is to loot or rob violently.

clue.text: Study bill for dispatch

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
a bill is a poster or sign

explanation.surface: Examine an invoice before posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to send off or hand over goods.

clue.text: Paper clip that will to keep things secure

definitions.text: that will to keep things secure

parts.note: the press means the newspapers
a clip is a device that fastens things together

explanation.surface: A stationery clip used to hold documents firmly together.
explanation.definitionFit: A popper or snap stud that keeps clothing closed securely.
